message.content:
Below are two ways to create a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**:

| Method | What you’ll run | Where you’ll run it |
|--------|-----------------|---------------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your terminal (or Cloud Shell) |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/.../zones/.../instances` | Any HTTP client (curl, Postman, Python, etc.) |

> **NOTE**  
> *Google Cloud does not use the term “EC2”; that’s AWS. In GCP the equivalent is a Compute Engine instance.*  
> *The RTX A6000 GPU is available as `nvidia-tesla-a6000`.*

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Pick a project, zone, and instance name
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"

# 2️⃣  Pick a machine type (e.g., 8 vCPU, 32 GB RAM)
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"

# 3️⃣  Pick the GPU count (max 8 per zone for RTX A6000)
GPU_COUNT=1

# 4️⃣  Pick the boot disk image (Ubuntu 20.04 LTS)
IMAGE="ubuntu-os-cloud/ubuntu-2004-lts"

# 5️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE_TYPE" \
  --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform" \
  --tags="http-server,https-server" \
  --service-account="default"
```

### What the command does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & RAM allocation |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU |
| `--image-project` / `--image-family` | Boot disk image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--boot-disk-type` | SSD for better I/O |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Optional script that runs on first boot |
| `--scopes` | Permissions for the instance |
| `--tags` | Network tags (e.g., allow HTTP/HTTPS) |
| `--service-account` | Which SA the instance uses |

> **Prerequisites**  
> *Make sure the Compute Engine API is enabled.*  
> *Ensure you have the GPU quota for the zone (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`).*  
> *If you’re using a custom service account, grant it the `Compute Admin` role or the minimal scopes needed.*

---

## 2. REST API (JSON)

Below is a minimal JSON payload you can POST to the Compute Engine API. Replace the placeholders with your own values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### How to POST it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

> **Authentication** – The example uses the Application Default Credentials (`gcloud auth application-default`).  
> **Quota** – Verify you have GPU quota for `nvidia-tesla-a6000` in the chosen zone.  
> **Error handling** – If the request fails, check the error message for missing quotas, invalid accelerator type, or insufficient permissions.

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After creation, you can verify the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=my-gcp-project \
  --zone=us-central1-a \
  --format="table(name, status, machineType, accelerators[*].type, accelerators[*].count)"
```

You should see something like:

```
NAME                STATUS   MACHINE_TYPE          ACCELERATORS
rtx-a6000-ubuntu    RUNNING  n1-standard-8         nvidia-tesla-a6000:1
```

---

### TL;DR

- **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator="type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1" --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts`
- **REST**: POST the JSON payload above to `https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/.../zones/.../instances`.

Both methods will give you a Compute Engine VM with an RTX A6000 GPU and Ubuntu 20.04 LTS. Happy GPU‑computing!
